questions.question: Which film has grossed the most money worldwide (as of 2024)?
questions.fun_fact: James Cameron's Avatar grossed over $2.9 billion, making it the highest-grossing film of all time — Cameron also holds third place with Titanic.

questions.question: Which video game is the best-selling of all time?
questions.fun_fact: Minecraft has sold over 300 million copies. It was originally developed by a single person — Swedish developer Markus 'Notch' Persson.

questions.question: Which song was the first YouTube video to reach one billion views?
questions.fun_fact: Gangnam Style hit a billion views in 2012 and actually overflowed YouTube's view counter, which could only count up to 2.1 billion at the time.

questions.question: What was the first fully computer-animated feature film?
questions.fun_fact: Toy Story was released in 1995 and produced by Pixar. Steve Jobs funded the studio and saved it from bankruptcy multiple times before the film became a massive hit.

questions.question: Which band has sold the most albums worldwide?
questions.fun_fact: The Beatles have sold an estimated 600 million records. Their active career lasted only about eight years — from 1962 to 1970.

questions.question: Which TV series holds the record for the most Emmy wins for a drama?
questions.fun_fact: Game of Thrones won 59 Emmys in total. Despite the controversial final season, it remains the most awarded drama series in Emmy history.

questions.question: Which actor was awarded a posthumous Oscar for playing the Joker?
questions.fun_fact: Heath Ledger died in January 2008, six months before The Dark Knight premiered. He locked himself in a hotel room for weeks to prepare for the role.

questions.question: What was Nintendo before it became a video game company?
questions.fun_fact: Nintendo was founded in 1889 and made traditional Japanese hanafuda playing cards. It took nearly 100 years before the company became a video game giant.

questions.question: How was nearly all of Toy Story 2 saved from accidental deletion?

answers.text: A backup on an employee's home computer saved the film
The film had to be completely re-animated
An IT specialist recovered the data

questions.fun_fact: A mistyped delete command wiped 90% of the film's data. Technical director Galyn Susman happened to have a copy on her home computer because she was working from home after having a baby.

questions.question: Which streaming service produced the first series to win an Emmy for Best Drama?
questions.fun_fact: Hulu's The Handmaid's Tale won the first streaming Emmy for Best Drama in 2017. Netflix won many Emmys with The Crown but claimed that award later.

questions.question: Which artist has the most number-one hits on the US Billboard charts?
questions.fun_fact: The Beatles hold the record with 20 number-one hits in the US. On a single day in April 1964, they simultaneously occupied all top 5 spots in the Billboard Hot 100.

questions.question: Which film won the very first Oscar for Best Picture?
questions.fun_fact: Wings won at the first Oscar ceremony in 1929. The entire event lasted only 15 minutes, and the winners were announced three months in advance.

questions.question: In which country was Tetris invented?
questions.fun_fact: Tetris was created in 1985 by Russian programmer Alexei Pajitnov in Moscow. Due to Soviet law, he received no income from his game for many years.

questions.question: Which animated series has aired continuously on US television since 1989?
questions.fun_fact: The Simpsons is the longest-running American animated primetime series. Matt Groening sketched the characters in just 15 minutes in a producer's waiting room.

questions.question: Which book is the best-selling after the Bible?

answers.text: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone

questions.fun_fact: Don Quixote by Miguel de Cervantes was published in 1605 and has sold an estimated 500 million copies. It is considered the first modern novel in world literature.

questions.question: Which actress was the first woman to gross one billion dollars at the box office?
questions.fun_fact: Emma Watson reached this milestone largely through the Harry Potter films. She was just 11 years old when the first film was released.

questions.question: What was the title of the first video ever uploaded to YouTube?
questions.fun_fact: The 18-second video 'Me at the zoo' shows YouTube co-founder Jawed Karim in front of elephants at San Diego Zoo. It was uploaded on 23 April 2005.

questions.question: Which famous actor turned down the role of Gandalf in The Lord of the Rings?
questions.fun_fact: Sean Connery declined because he didn't understand the screenplay. He was reportedly offered 15% of box office revenues — that would have been over $400 million.

questions.question: Which instrument plays the iconic Jaws theme?
questions.fun_fact: John Williams' iconic two-note motif is played by cellos. Director Steven Spielberg initially thought Williams was joking when he heard the simple theme for the first time.

questions.question: What colour was the original iPhone released in 2007?
questions.fun_fact: Steve Jobs unveiled the first iPhone in January 2007. The prototype on stage kept crashing, so the team carefully ordered the demo to show each feature only once.

questions.question: Which Disney film was the first to gross over $1 billion?
questions.fun_fact: Toy Story 3 crossed the billion-dollar mark in 2010 as the first pure Disney/Pixar film to do so — fittingly, a film about growing up for an audience that had grown up with the franchise.

questions.question: What is the famous Konami Code hidden in many video games?

answers.text: Up, Up, Down, Down, Left, Right, Left, Right, B, A
Left, Right, Left, Right, Up, Down, Up, Down, A, B
Up, Down, Up, Down, Left, Right, B, A, Start

questions.fun_fact: The Konami Code was invented in 1986 by developer Kazuhisa Hashimoto for the game Gradius because he found it too difficult. It now appears in hundreds of games and even websites.

questions.question: Which rapper was a ballet dancer before his music career?
questions.fun_fact: Tupac attended the Baltimore School for the Arts, where he studied ballet, acting, and poetry. He even played the Mouse in a production of The Nutcracker.

questions.question: Which animal inspired the Pokémon character Pikachu?
questions.fun_fact: Pikachu's designer Atsuko Nishida was inspired by the pika, a small mammal found in Asian mountains. The name combines 'pika' with 'chu', the Japanese onomatopoeia for an electric crackle.

questions.question: Which famous TV series was originally developed as 'The Untitled Lindelof Project'?
questions.fun_fact: Lost was developed at record speed: just 12 weeks from first concept to finished pilot. The pilot cost $13 million — the most expensive series pilot at the time.

questions.question: Which song has the most streams on Spotify (as of 2024)?
questions.fun_fact: Blinding Lights spent over 90 weeks on the Billboard Hot 100 — an absolute record. The Weeknd drew inspiration from 80s synth-pop for the sound.

questions.question: Which country is the Netflix series Squid Game set in?
questions.fun_fact: Squid Game became the most-watched Netflix series ever. Director Hwang Dong-hyuk wrote the screenplay in 2009 but couldn't find a studio willing to produce it for over a decade.

questions.question: Which superhero was originally conceived as a villain?
questions.fun_fact: Wolverine first appeared in 1974 as an opponent of the Hulk. He was intended as a one-off antagonist but became so popular he turned hero and eventually the most iconic X-Men member.

questions.question: Which famous director made the Thriller music video for Michael Jackson?
questions.fun_fact: The Thriller video cost $500,000 — the most expensive music video of its time. At 14 minutes long, it was the first music video inducted into the Library of Congress.

questions.question: Which was the first video game played in space?
questions.fun_fact: Russian cosmonaut Alexander Serebrov played Tetris on a Game Boy aboard the Mir space station in 1993. That Game Boy was later auctioned for $1,220.

questions.question: Which actress has appeared in the most episodes of a single TV series?
questions.fun_fact: Mariska Hargitay has played Olivia Benson in Law & Order: SVU since 1999 — over 500 episodes. Her mother was actress Jayne Mansfield.

questions.question: What was the first word ever sent over the internet?
questions.fun_fact: In 1969, 'Login' was intended to be sent, but the computer crashed after 'L' and 'O'. The internet's first word was an accidental 'Lo' — as in 'Lo and behold'.

questions.question: Which streaming service has the most subscribers worldwide (as of 2024)?
questions.fun_fact: Netflix started in 1997 as a DVD-by-mail rental service. Co-founder Reed Hastings reportedly got the idea after paying a $40 late fee for an Apollo 13 VHS tape.

questions.question: Which Lord of the Rings character was originally scripted to die in the battle at the Black Gate?
questions.fun_fact: Peter Jackson actually filmed scenes of Aragorn fighting Sauron and dying. The sequence was cut because it deviated too far from Tolkien's story.

questions.question: Which musician has won the most Grammy Awards?
questions.fun_fact: Beyoncé has won over 30 Grammys, making her the most decorated artist in Grammy history. She was only nine years old at her first audition.

questions.question: Which social media network was the first to reach one billion users?
questions.fun_fact: Facebook hit one billion monthly active users in 2012. Mark Zuckerberg coded the first version in just two weeks in his Harvard dorm room.

questions.question: What is the name of the fictional language created for Game of Thrones?
questions.fun_fact: Linguist David J. Peterson created Dothraki with over 4,000 words and its own grammar. He beat out 30 other applicants who also wanted to develop the language.

questions.question: Which famous fictional character is described as blonde in the books but portrayed as brunette in the films?
questions.fun_fact: In Ian Fleming's novels, James Bond is described as dark-haired with a scar. It wasn't until Daniel Craig in 2006 that Bond became blonde — and Fleming would have hated it.

questions.question: Which famous meme came from a photo of a perpetually grumpy-looking cat?
questions.fun_fact: Grumpy Cat (real name Tardar Sauce) had feline dwarfism, which caused her permanently grumpy expression. Her owner reportedly earned over $100 million from the cat.

questions.question: How many books are in the Harry Potter series?
questions.fun_fact: J.K. Rowling was rejected by 12 publishers before Bloomsbury published Harry Potter. The editor only agreed because his eight-year-old daughter loved the first chapter.

questions.question: Which actor has appeared in the most Marvel Cinematic Universe films?
questions.fun_fact: Samuel L. Jackson appeared as Nick Fury in over 11 MCU films. He signed an unprecedented nine-film contract with Marvel — the longest actor contract in Hollywood history.

questions.question: What is true about the first emoji ever created?

answers.text: It was part of a set of 176 emojis

questions.fun_fact: The first 176 emojis were designed in 1999 by Japanese designer Shigetaka Kurita for mobile carrier NTT DoCoMo. Each emoji was only 12×12 pixels. The originals are now displayed in New York's MoMA.

questions.question: Which legendary video game character was named after the landlord of a Nintendo warehouse?
questions.fun_fact: Mario was named after Mario Segale, the landlord of Nintendo's US warehouse. Segale once stormed in demanding overdue rent — and inadvertently inspired the world's most famous game character.

questions.question: Which film was the first to be released with the Dolby Atmos sound system?
questions.fun_fact: Pixar's Brave was the first theatrical film with Dolby Atmos in 2012. The system uses up to 128 separate audio channels and can position sounds three-dimensionally in a room.

questions.question: Which famous musician worked as a part-time baggage handler before becoming famous?
questions.fun_fact: Freddie Mercury worked at London's Heathrow Airport as a baggage handler and sold second-hand clothes at Kensington Market before Queen broke through.

questions.question: Which word was Oxford Dictionary's 'Word of the Year' in 2013?
questions.fun_fact: Usage of the word 'selfie' rose 17,000% in 2013. The oldest known selfie actually dates back to 1839 — a photograph taken by chemist Robert Cornelius.

questions.question: How many seasons did the original Star Trek series have?
questions.fun_fact: The original series ran for only three seasons (1966–1969) and was cancelled due to poor ratings. It became a cult hit in reruns and launched a multi-billion-dollar franchise.

questions.question: What was the subject of one of the first widely shared GIFs on the internet?
questions.fun_fact: The GIF format was developed by CompuServe in 1987. One of the first widely shared GIFs showed a spinning aeroplane. The debate over pronunciation ('GIF' vs 'JIF') continues to this day.

questions.question: Which Hollywood star was a bodybuilder and won the Mr. Universe title before becoming an actor?
questions.fun_fact: Arnold Schwarzenegger won his first Mr. Universe title at just 20 years old. He sometimes trained so hard he passed out in the gym.

questions.question: What colour was the dress that divided the internet in 2015 (#TheDress)?

answers.text: It was actually blue and black
It was actually white and gold
It was actually blue and brown

questions.fun_fact: The viral dress phenomenon of 2015 was studied by scientists and published in academic journals. The differing perceptions arise from how the brain compensates for ambient lighting.
